title: Deterministic plotting gallery evidence
objective: Generate and validate a compact cross-dimensional Sage plotting gallery with semantic, geometry, responsive, contrast, alt-text, SVG/PNG, and performance evidence plus explicit Wolfram/MATLAB placeholders and a human-review protocol

oracles: Checked deterministic PlotSpec/Plotly fixtures and structural SVG/PNG rendering evidence
WCAG contrast thresholds and responsive viewport invariants

handoff.summary: Commit 89667827 adds a deterministic gallery generator and compact checked evidence for ten actual PlotSpec/Plotly figures: semantic Sage 2D and 3D slices across notebook, presentation, publication, dark, and high-contrast themes. It validates stable geometry and trace families, theme and rendered-layer contrast, explicit semantic alt text, three responsive viewports, structural SVG/PNG properties, output and wall-time ceilings, and a detailed human-review protocol without committing image blobs or pixel hashes. A real local Plotly 3.7.0/Chromium run found zero viewport overflow, vector paths in representative 2D SVG, one correctly disclosed embedded raster image in 3D SVG, valid 800x600 PNGs, and no DOM accessible name despite the available semantic alt text.
risks: The current Plotly display bridge does not attach PlotSpec alt text to a stable DOM accessible name; the gallery records this as product debt rather than treating semantic alt text alone as an accessibility pass.
Wolfram and MATLAB gallery cases are explicit pending-integration placeholders until their independent frontend branches land; no compatibility evidence is fabricated.

The required integration tier ran 436 tests with 397 passes and 38 failures. All observed plotting agent API, presentation/composition, PlotSpec, surface, theme, coverage, graphics, graphics3d, and export suites passed. Failures were outside this claimed slice and predominantly came from absent or stale compiled native artifacts, missing compiler task-runtime output, multiprocessing fallout, and timing thresholds; public sparse random also hit its existing timeout.
Chromium is an optional tested capability. Hosts without it still validate deterministic semantic, geometry, contrast, alt-text, budget, and checked structural evidence, but skip a fresh live render.
next_steps: Register test/plot-gallery-quality.cjs in the central Node test manifest; this lane intentionally has no manifest claim.
After Wolfram and MATLAB adapters merge, replace their pending placeholders with equivalent frontend-produced PlotSpecs and add those fixtures to the same structural checks.
Connect PlotSpec alt text to a stable role and accessible name in the display integration, then update the honest browser-DOM expectation from debt to a tested pass.
Use the documented keyboard, screen-reader, touch, visual-craft, and export protocol before plotting releases and after Plotly or theme changes.
